name: Cube-Completion Width Laws
statement: For every nonempty $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, $\sigma_{\square}(C)\geq\sigma(C)$, and $\sigma_{\square}(C)=0$ exactly when both $C$ and its cube complement are dismantlable ample (the empty complement is allowed). Nonempty pc-minors cannot increase $\sigma_{\square}$; on disjoint coordinate sets, $\sigma_{\square}(C\times D)=\max\{\sigma_{\square}(C),\sigma_{\square}(D)\}$. Cube symmetries and constant coordinates preserve the value. If $C^{\mathrm c}$ is dismantlable ample, then $\sigma_{\square}(C)=\sigma(C)$.
proof: The prescribed initial segment gives the first inequality. A zero-width full-cube order makes $C$ dismantlable; reading the suffix backwards gives a zero-width order of the complement because complements of ample prefixes are ample. Conversely, append the reverse of a zero-width complement order to an optimal order of $C$. The pc-minor and product laws follow by applying the paired prescribed-width laws to $(\{0,1\}^X,C)$, while a constant coordinate is a product with a singleton.
